label: The AskUserQuestion ban
gloss: A prose rule in home's CLAUDE.md, a deny in two repos' project settings that is read only when that repo is the root, a user-scope deny the old setup script writes, and the plugin guard. The guard is meant to replace the user deny.

label: Writing rules
gloss: The user-scope CLAUDE.md, the account preferences and QUALIFIED-WRITING.md all state rules about plain words and the em dash, in three different wordings.

label: The HTML house style
gloss: The plugin's html-style skill and an older claude.ai upload named daisy-alpine both reach Code sessions and describe the same stack differently; the preferences restate it a third time.

label: How the conventions arrive
gloss: The plugin delivers them; each repo's CLAUDE.md also explains that delivery, so one mechanism is described in several places.

label: Keeping the plugin current
gloss: Until the setup script is replaced, two refreshers run: the old user-scope refresh-portable.sh and the plugin's own refresher.

label: Where sessions are recorded
gloss: The environment variable, a checkout's sessionsStore declaration and the hard-coded default name the store in that order; the store's own manifest makes it findable.

label: Pull-request behaviour
gloss: The harness's own PR instructions, the account's automatic draft PRs, the surfacing course and the send-later guard all shape what a session does with a PR.

label: GitHub access
gloss: Two GitHub MCP servers reach the same repos, and the session's repo scope is set separately from either.

label: What the skill listing costs
gloss: About 30 skills arrive twice, once from the plugin and once as claude.ai uploads, and every description is paid for in every session.

label: Repo session scripts
gloss: Each checkout's session-*.sh files run through the plugin's dispatcher rather than from settings, so they fire whatever the root.

label: Showing a change
gloss: How to link or render a change is stated in web-tools' CLAUDE.md, in home's CLAUDE.md and in the surfacing docs.

label: Editing governing documents
gloss: A commit gate and an edit-time warning both require specific permission for documentation edits.
